selection: Six distinct mineral species and one mining-generated liquid resource extend primary-evidence coverage. Montroseite and paramontroseite retain inferred natural weathering; paramontroseite also has a separate abiotic heating experiment. Ulexite has qualified humidity-driven rehydration, while kernite, phosphophyllite and laueite support identity and crystal-chemistry records. Acid mine drainage has two separately scoped laboratory microbial treatment studies; its Silva2019 experiment is already represented by the covellite product record and is not independent replication.

source_issues.body:
The new `data/records/acid-mine-drainage.yaml` preserves two laboratory studies at their supported scope. Its remaining evidence gaps cannot be repaired by inferring missing measurements.

In Silva et al. (2019), DOI 10.3390/met9020206, the collected solid is assigned to covellite, but Table 3 Cu/S wt% entries sum above 100% and the text calls mass-entry ratios molar. Final aqueous copper, collected solid mass and a closed copper balance are not supplied. This same experiment is already represented in the covellite record and must not be counted as independent replication.

In Akinpelu et al. (2021), DOI 10.1016/j.heliyon.2021.e07241 (PMC8215182), the full published article, original figures and Table S1 mention a consortium-free control without supplying its numerical outcomes. Table 5's exact sampling day/fraction, daily feed/withdrawal balance and nutrient-medium contributions remain unresolved. Concentration decreases do not establish isolated metal recovery or causal benefit over matched controls. The public inventory for cited study SRP149893 returns one wastewater-metagenome run and does not map both Sa/Sb labels to distinct runs.

Evidence: `research/sources/round101-amd/20261015T193414Z-source-investigation.{json,md}`; full-source acquisition and failure receipts are retained there. Bounded de-duplication included hidden/ignored local files and all 257 GitHub issue title/body entries; comments were not exhaustively searched. No existing issue covers these exact experiments and gaps.

Follow-up acceptance:

- Locate published or repository-hosted corrected composition data, actual numerical control outputs and phase-resolved mass accounting.
- Resolve the 2021 sampling schedule/fraction, feed/withdrawal volumes and Sa/Sb-to-run mapping before adding quantitative or member-specific claims.
- Preserve the current qualifications until independent evidence supports a change; add immutable EDIT history and a fresh scientific review of any changed record.
- Do not infer yield from aqueous depletion or contact authors without separate authorization.

This is an open source-evidence follow-up, not a defect concealed in the scoped record and not a prerequisite for retaining the supported narrower observations.
source_issues.title: Resolve acid mine drainage control, balance and sequence-sample gaps

source_issues.body:
Curetti and Pavese (2023), DOI 10.5194/ejm-35-373-2023, provides primary evidence for oxidative breakdown of a natural Fe-rich paramontroseite specimen. The new `data/records/paramontroseite.yaml` retains a specific unresolved discrepancy: Section 3.2 assigns approximately 65 wt% to Fe2V4O13 and 35 wt% to V2O5, while labeled Figure 7 depicts V2O5 as the larger final product and retains calcite. Exact fractions and their denominator are therefore not accepted as recovery yields.

The inspected full original, XML and publisher Tables 1-4 are documented in `research/sources/round101-vanadium/20261015T193316Z.{json,md}`. CCDC 2212426/2212427 acquisition did not succeed by the logged routes. The approximate Al-free reaction formula, measured average chemistry and refined occupancies are distinct quantities; this natural specimen is not pure VO2.

Follow-up acceptance:

- Obtain an authoritative correction or phase-fraction dataset that reconciles the final product assignments, retained calcite and normalization.
- Acquire and inspect the deposited structural data through a supported public route before claiming independent model verification.
- Keep powder heating, separate six-hour crystal treatments and laser-altered Raman observations distinct.
- Update only claims directly resolved by the evidence, retaining append-only history and a new exact-state scientific review.

Hidden/ignored local source boundaries and the 257-issue title/body inventory were searched before creating this follow-up. No existing issue specifically covers this discrepancy. It remains an evidence question; the current record explicitly preserves it.
source_issues.title: Reconcile paramontroseite thermal product fractions and deposited models

source_issues.body:
The new `data/records/laueite.yaml` supports species identity and qualified natural epitaxy while preserving unresolved composition/model questions in Grey et al. (2025), DOI 10.1180/mgm.2025.21.

The paper's EDS-derived metal composition (scaled to three metal atoms) differs from the simplified refined Mn/Mg occupancy. Its deposited laueite checkCIF report contains three A-level displacement alerts, missing-hydrogen and formula/Z reporting alerts, and lacks structure factors for full checks. Those alerts limit detailed atomistic interpretation; they do not by themselves negate mineral identity or epitaxial orientation. Baur (1969) independently proposed partial Mn(III) occupancy from older bond lengths rather than a direct oxidation-state assay.

Evidence: complete primary originals, both deposited CIFs and both checkCIF reports, documented in `research/sources/round101-phosphates/20261015T193202Z-source-investigation.{json,md}`. The current IMA ideal formula remains distinct from specimen chemistry and refined scattering models.

Follow-up acceptance:

- Locate complete diffraction/structure-factor data and a defensible re-refinement or authoritative explanation of the displacement and reporting alerts.
- Reconcile specimen composition, site occupancy and hydrogen/valence assignments with direct evidence where available.
- Preserve the historical competing interpretation and avoid inferring transformation or microbial causality from natural epitaxy.
- Any record change needs canonical EDIT history and an independent review of its final bytes.

Bounded searches included hidden/ignored local files and all 257 issue title/body entries. No existing laueite-specific issue was found. This tracks unresolved source evidence already qualified in the record, not a claim that the record itself omits these limits.
source_issues.title: Resolve laueite composition and deposited diffraction-model qualifications

publication_review_issue.body:
Independent publication review found that the redox category introduces all its mechanisms as enzymatic or cell-surface reactions, although its current 57 records include 15 explicitly abiotic mechanisms (60 mechanisms total). New montroseite and paramontroseite records make the mismatch concrete; older anilite and other records already have the same boundary.

Maintained owner: `scripts/render_pages.py`, `PROCESS_BLURBS['redox_transformation']`. Generated output: `pages/processes/redox_transformation.html`.

Independent initial audit: `reviews/publication/20261015-round101/20261015T193803Z-redox-display-initial.{json,md}`. Stable issue key: `CMMMech:publication-redox-blurb-microbial-scope`; severity minor. The scientific owners already state microbial involvement correctly.

Acceptance:

- Replace the biological-only category introduction with neutral oxidation-reduction wording, stating that microbial involvement is specified in each record.
- Regenerate the site without changing mechanism counts or scientific records.
- Run the existing rendering tests and freshness check.
- Save an independent successor review linked to the initial finding, confirming exact corrected source/output hashes and unchanged scientific owners.

This is distinct from closed homepage issue #368: its fix covered the homepage, while this finding concerns category-specific prose. No new record/schema behavior is needed for this wording correction.
publication_review_issue.title: Correct biological-only introduction on the redox category page
